Principal's Message
I am truly honored and feel deeply privileged to serve as the Principal of Indira Gandhi College, Boitamari, which was
established on 10th September 1995.

I would like to take this opportunity to express my heartfelt gratitude to the Governing Body of Indira Gandhi College
for entrusting me with this noble responsibility. It is a great privilege to serve the community of Boitamari, Bongaigaon
(Assam), and contribute to the institution's growth and progress.

As the head of this institution, my ultimate ambition is to ignite the flame of success in the days to come. I firmly
believe that every challenge can be overcome through motivation, determination, dedication, and unwavering
commitment.

We, the Indira Gandhi College family, are devoted to embracing new challenges and pursuing success at every stage.
With unity, resilience, and a shared vision, we shall strive to bring glory and excellence to our institution.
 "I personally believe that teaching no longer is just transmitting knowledge. It is, succinctly speaking, about forming,
reshaping, and transforming young minds. According to the NEP 2020, it is the acquisition of knowledge and skills,
building character, and enhancing the employability of our young talent so that they can efficiently face all challenges in
their careers and future.

With a vision of intense progress through positivity and a mission of extreme achievement through harmony, I join my
hands with all the teaching and non-teaching staff as well as students to take the College towards a better tomorrow.

A heterogeneous group of learners and knowledge seekers, with a wide spectrum of aspirations, aptitudes, and choices,
is attracted to the College because it offers students good infrastructural facilities along with a competent, dedicated,
well-experienced, and excellent faculty who strive for the all-round development of each and every student. The well-
qualified faculty of the College are always inspiring students with their multifaceted personality."

In the same vein as NEP 2020, the College has always promoted the use of cutting-edge, technology-based education
policies. This is evident from the fact that most classrooms are equipped with built-in audio-visual systems and internet
connectivity, which can be utilized during lectures.

Indeed, the efforts of our teaching staff to continuously enhance their knowledge and skills—coupled with
encouragement and support from the management—form an ongoing process that fosters a dynamic and vibrant
academic atmosphere on our College campus.

The College campus is green and thriving, thanks to the untiring personal interest, physical presence, and guidance of
our Honorable President of the Governing Body, Sri Kamal Kishore Adhikary. His dynamic, versatile, and visionary
leadership has led to remarkable growth, and I am confident that we will reach new heights in the near future.

Furthermore, various college activities such as cultural programs, games and sports, educational tours, etc., help build
bonds among students. These activities not only minimize the gap between staff and students but also build a
metaphysical and moral bridge that fosters mutual respect and understanding.

We, the entire family of Indira Gandhi College, assume moral and social responsibility in all our activities as a matter of
conscience. We dedicate ourselves to improving the quality of life in our own way by adopting the highest standards in
education to meet the demands of the 21st-century world.

In other words, the core vision of the College is to reshape and impart quality education to students so they are prepared
to face new challenges in their careers and lives, and to become competent for the global job market.




                                                                             NarayanMedhi

                                                   About the College




Indira Gandhi College, Boitamari is located in the heart of Boitamari, adjacent to National Highway 17 (NH-17), and is one of
the prominent colleges in Assam. The college was established on September 10, 1995, and the foundation stone was laid by the
Honourable Chief Minister Hiteswar Saikia on the same day.

The college came into existence through the efforts of several local individuals and the then MLA Sri Chandan Kumar Sarkar of
Abhayapuri South L.A.C. The people from nearby areas such as Moligaon, Salbari, Dhakanabari, Bamunilam, Dhantola,
Jolakhata, Raghunandanpur, Barkhata, Kasharpara, Amguri, Bashbari, Dwenwangaon, Dhalagaon, Rashigaon, Bidyapur, Bahalpur,
Mulagaon, Khagarpur, Talguri, Panchagaon, and other adjoining regions contributed generously—despite economic hardship—to
make the dream of this college a reality.

The college is named after Smt. Indira Gandhi, former Prime Minister of India, who played a pivotal role in shaping a prosperous
India. It is situated in the North Salmara Sub-Division of Bongaigaon District. The natural beauty of the location is enhanced by
the presence of the Tunia River and the Bhairav Chura Hill behind it.

Initially established as a single-faculty Arts Degree College, it is affiliated with Gauhati University, Guwahati. Over time, the
college has expanded its reach in the field of higher education. A team of highly qualified and dedicated teachers imparts
knowledge using modern methods and techniques.

Since its inception, the college has faced many challenges. However, due to the tireless efforts of the college authorities, along with
the support of the teaching and non-teaching staff, students, and the local community, the college has grown steadily.

Today, the hallmark of Indira Gandhi College includes:

       Regular classes
       Good academic results
       Periodic evaluation
       Strict discipline
       A strong teacher-student relationship

         Four Year undergraduate programme (FYUGP)

         Core Courses + Common Courses


                                          1. CORE COURSES

Total Core Papers: 2. Subjects to be selected from the available options offered by the college.
In case of a Bachelor’s Degree in arts Stream, a student either chooses 1 Major &1 Minors
Or just 2 Minors from among the subjects.




                                          2. COMMON COURSES




         Four(4) Common Courses Compulsory for all.

              MDC                  AEC                     SEC                     VAC
                                    Multi-Disciplinary Courses (MDC):
These are 3-credit courses spanning five different subject groups:

   1.   Natural and Physical Sciences
   2.   Mathematics, Statistics, and Computer Applications
   3.   Library, Information, and Media Science
   4.   Commerce and Management
   5.   Humanities and Social Science

The level of these courses corresponds to Class XII.
Each student must take one course per semester in Semesters I, II, and III, totaling 9 credits (3 credits per course ×
3 semesters).




                                 Ability Enhancement Course (AEC):
This is an 8-credit course covering:

       Modern Indian Language (MIL)
       English Usage (Communication)

Each student must complete:

       Two papers of 4 credits each:
          o One in English Usage
          o One in MIL

Each 4-credit paper is split into two 2-credit sub-courses.

Schedule:

       MIL course is to be completed during Semesters I & V
       English Communication course is to be completed during Semesters II & VI



                                  Skill Enhancement Courses (SEC):
       Total Credit: 9
       All students must complete three skill enhancement courses, each worth 3 credits.
       These courses are to be completed in semesters 1, 2, and 3.


                                        Value-Added Courses (VAC):
       Total Credit: 6
       Students must take three courses, each of 2 credits, from any three of the following groups:
           1. Understanding India
           2. Environmental Science (one course from this group is compulsory unless the student is taking a core
               course in Environmental Science)
           3. Digital and Technological Solutions
           4. Health & Wellness
           5. Yoga Education
           6. Sports and Fitness
       These courses should be completed across semesters 1, 2, and 4.
                                                       Internship:
      Credit Allocation: 4
      The internship is typically carried out during the summer break between the 4th and 5th semesters.
      Credits are added to the 5th semester.
      If a student misses the internship at that time, they must complete it after the 6th semester (during the
       following summer break).
      In such cases, the 5th semester result will be marked as INCOMPLETE until the internship is completed.

        Program Outcomes: Four Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP)
(Offered by the Affiliating University: Gauhati University)

The undergraduate degree (UG) programme under the Four Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP) follows a
Choice-Based Credit System (CBCS) under the semester scheme.

Key features include:

      Multiple Exit Options:
          o After 2 semesters (1 year): Award of Certificate
          o After 4 semesters (2 years): Award of Diploma
          o After 6 semesters (3 years): Award of Undergraduate Degree with Major
          o Completion of all 8 semesters (4 years): Award of Honours/Research Degree (if applicable)
      Academic Year Structure:
          o Each academic year consists of two consecutive semesters: one Odd and one Even
          o Odd Semesters: First, Third, Fifth, and Seventh — conducted from July to December
          o Even Semesters: Second, Fourth, Sixth, and Eighth — conducted from January to June
 After completing the B.A. course, students are expected to acquire:

   1. Career Opportunities:
      After graduation, students have the opportunity to engage in employment in either the government or private
      sector, or they may choose to become entrepreneurs.
   2. Higher Education:
      They may pursue higher studies in their field of interest.
   3. Subject Knowledge:
      They acquire knowledge with relevant facts and figures related to subjects such as Geography, Languages,
      Political Science, etc.
   4. Literary and Societal Appreciation:
      They realize the importance of literature in terms of aesthetic, mental, moral, and intellectual development of an
      individual and, consequently, of society.
   5. Analytical Skills:
      They gain the analytical ability to examine literature and social issues, appreciate strengths, and suggest
      improvements for better outcomes.
   6. Broader Perspective:
      They are convinced that the study of literature and social sciences is not only beneficial to the individual and
      society but also helps make life more meaningful.

                                           College Code of Conduct
The Code of Conduct includes policies and rules that all students must follow to maintain discipline and ensure a safe
and respectful learning environment. The objective is to help students develop good habits, self-discipline, and
consideration for others, which will ultimately lead to a better future.

                                          Rules and Regulations:
   1. Punctuality:
       All students must arrive at the college on time. Latecomers will not be allowed to enter the college premises.
   2. Dress Code:
       Students must wear neat and clean attire. Scribbling on uniforms or improper wearing of uniforms is punishable.
   3. Prohibited Items:
       Sharp objects or any kind of weapons are strictly prohibited on college premises.
   4. Vehicle Rules:
       Students are not allowed to bring vehicles to college without proper documents such as Driving License (DL),
       Registration Certificate (RC), Insurance, Pollution Certificate, and Helmet.
   5. Class Periods:
       Students are not allowed to visit the canteen during scheduled class hours.
   6. Classroom Conduct:
       No form of gathering or celebration is allowed inside the classroom.
   7. Attendance Requirement:
       Students must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance to be eligible for the final semester examinations.
   8. Leaving Campus:
       Students are not allowed to leave the college campus during college hours without prior permission from the
       concerned authority.
   9. Anti-Bullying Policy:
       Bullying in any form is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated.
   10. Noise Control:
       Whistling and shouting within the college premises are not permitted.
   11. Property Damage:
       Any act of damaging or destroying college property is punishable.
   12. Unauthorized Gatherings:
       Organizing meetings or processions without proper permission from higher authorities is not allowed.
   13. Substance Prohibition:
       Smoking, chewing tobacco, consumption of alcohol, or use of any drug-related substances is strictly prohibited.
   14. Recording Restrictions:
       Audio or video recording within college premises is not allowed without prior permission from the higher
       authorities.
                                          Anti-Ragging Cell Overview
Definition of Ragging:
Ragging is any disorderly conduct, whether through words (spoken or written) or actions, that results in teasing,
treating, or handling a fresher or junior student rudely. It may involve rowdy or undisciplined behavior that causes or is
likely to cause annoyance, hardship, psychological harm, or fear. This behavior often leads to a sense of shame or
embarrassment and can severely impact the physical or mental well-being of the affected student, sometimes resulting
in depression, anxiety, or even suicide.


                         Guidelines for a Positive College Environment:
   1. Respectful Behavior: Students must behave respectfully at all times.
   2. Zero Tolerance for Harassment or Bullying: The college will not tolerate any form of harassment or bullying.
   3. Constructive Conflict Resolution: Encourage methods to resolve conflicts peacefully and respectfully.
   4. Adherence to Academic Integrity: Students are expected to uphold the highest standards of academic
      integrity.
   5. Promotion of Diversity and Inclusion: A diverse and inclusive environment will be promoted for all students.
   6. Professional Conduct: All interactions, whether with peers or faculty, should maintain professionalism.


                                   Functions of the Anti-Ragging Cell:
       Prohibit Ragging: Ensure that no student indulges in behavior that teases, treats rudely, or bullies juniors or
        fresher students.
       Campus Vigilance: Maintain a ragging-free campus environment.
       Dissemination of Information: Inform students about anti-ragging rules and laws, including those issued by
        the Supreme Court of India, the High Court of Guwahati, and the University Grants Commission (UGC).
       Immediate Action: Address any ragging complaints promptly, taking appropriate action as per the advice of the
        committee.
       Awareness Campaigns: Raise awareness among students about the harmful effects and legal consequences
        of ragging.
       Continuous Vigilance: Regularly monitor and ensure that no ragging incidents occur.
       Meetings: The Anti-Ragging Cell will conduct executive meetings three times a year to review and update
        policies.

                                               Central Library:

Indira Gandhi College Central Library was established in 1995, the same year the college was founded. The library
is fully automated, with the integration of the KOHA library management system in 2024. It includes a digital
library section that provides access to various e-resources, such as previous question papers, college journals,
magazines, newsletters, and more. The library holds a collection of over 5,000 copies of text and reference books,
covering a wide range of subjects. Additionally, the library regularly collects feedback from users regarding its
services. Library membership is compulsory for all students.


                                                   Library Timings

                                            Onworkingdays—9:00A.M to4:30P.M


                                           1. Digital Classroom
The college is equipped with a modern digital classroom facility. It enables students to engage in interactive
discussions, share perspectives, and collaborate on projects with peers from diverse cultural backgrounds.

                                            2. Add-On Courses
The college offers various Add-On Diploma and Certificate courses across departments for enrolled students.
The primary objective of these courses is to add value, agility, and academic strength to students within the same
duration as their regular degree programs.

                                      3. Educational Excursions
Students are actively encouraged to participate in educational excursions. An environmental excursion is
mandatory for all 4th-semester degree students.
                           4. Career Counselling and Placement Cell
The Career Counselling and Placement Cell provides expert guidance to students regarding their career paths. It
organizes sessions on current affairs, general knowledge, and other career-oriented topics by distinguished
professionals.




                                               5. Scholarships
The following scholarships are available to eligible students:

      National Merit Scholarship
      Scholarships for Students from Backward and Minority Communities




                                            6. Canteen Facilities
Indira Gandhi College provides canteen facilities for students, staff, and authorized visitors. The canteen includes
a cooking area and a designated food service zone where meals and snacks are served.



                                             7. College Uniform
Wearing the college uniform is mandatory on all working days. Students without proper uniform will not be
allowed to enter the campus.

      For Boys: Light Pink Formal Shirt and Black Trousers
      For Girls: Light Pink Kurta, Black Pyjama, and Dupatta
